text:
Maya (Sales): FYI - Umbra just confirmed they'll run a 2-week POC next week. They want to validate a custom Aurora-Alpha-30B variant and ask about onboarding timeline and blockers.

Ethan (SE): Awesome — do we have the model artifact + tokenizer details from them? main concerns will be quantization format + kv-cache layout.

Maya (Sales): They uploaded an S3 link in the ticket. Says it's a 'q4_0' quant variant with a custom BPE tokenizer, some positional embedding differences. Also asked about dedicated capacity pricing and SLA for low-latency inference.

Priya (ML Eng): q4_0 should be fine but we need to check fused-kernel compatibility. If tokenizer differs we may need to ship a tokenizer adapter or surface a tokenizer container. Two quick checks I want to run:
- verify tokenizer vocab mapping (special tokens)
- run a KV-cache warmup trace to confirm layout and key dtype (float16 vs int8)

Ethan (SE): Agree. From ops side we also need to know whether they require KMS-backed keys for model weights and whether vectors/inputs must be excluded from logs. That affects Private vs Dedicated pricing.

Maya (Sales): Umbra asked for KMS + SOC2 info in their security questionnaire. They also want to know if we support explicit deletion of request logs per contract.

Jamal (Security): We can provide KMS integration (AWS KMS / Google KMS) for Private and Dedicated. For hosted API, customer-managed KMS isn't available but we support envelope encryption and customer-controlled retention windows. Deletion-on-demand is an enterprise flow (requires Private or Dedicated + legal addendum).

Ava (Legal): Noted — we'll need the exact retention duration in the SOW. Also request: Umbra asked for a clause for immutable logs for 90 days then purge? We should propose standard entitlements: 90-day audit logs retention by default for Dedicated, extendable via add-on.

Ethan (SE): For the model compat tests I can run the following locally if someone confirms we can pull from their S3. Minimal test plan:
```
1) Tokenize sample corpus -> compare token counts vs their baseline
2) Load quantized weights -> run 10 warmup inferences -> capture latency and kv cache usage
3) Try batch sizes [1,4,8] on our T4/RTX8000 template and measure p50/p95
```
I'll upload results to the ticket.

Priya (ML Eng): Also adding: if tokenizer mapping differs for unknown token ids we should provide an adapter layer that normalizes special tokens (e.g., <s>, </s>, <pad>). That typically costs ~1 dev-day to implement and validate.

Maya (Sales): Umbra asked pricing: they want an estimate for a 2-week POC on Dedicated (8x A10g equiv). What numbers do we ballpark? They also asked about a follow-on pilot for production if POC passes.

Ethan (SE): For Dedicated POC: assume reserved short-term rate + setup. Quick ballpark: $18k/week for 8 GPUs reserved (depends on region). Add model onboarding support (2 dev-days + SE time) ~ $6k one-time. Pilot pricing would be contract-negotiated; we can show TCO based on token rates vs latency SLA.

Maya (Sales): I'll give them the ballpark and say final quote after compatibility pass.

Jamal (Security): Two security Qs I need answered from Umbra: do they require data plane traffic over private peering (VPC) and do they require HSM-backed KMS? If yes -> Private deployment required.

Maya (Sales): I'll ask.

Ava (Legal): Also confirm whether model weights are considered customer IP in their view. If they claim ownership, we need to add IP handling language and possibly a storage isolation clause.

Priya (ML Eng): Technical note: if the model uses nonstandard rotary embeddings we'll need to validate kernel support in our runtime. That can be a binary blocker for q4_0 conversion. If blocked, fallback options: 1) run in FP16 unquantized for POC (higher cost) 2) ask vendor for an alternative quant version.

Ethan (SE): To speed things up, can we get Umbra to run a small sanity script we provide that prints tokenizer tokens + a single forward pass output hash? If they deliver that, it greatly shortens onboarding.

Maya (Sales): I'll send that script now.

deploy-bot: Ticket #S-4821 created -> Umbra POC: Aurora-Alpha-30B custom variant. Owner: Ethan (SE). Priority: high.

Ethan (SE): Thanks — I'll kick off the runs once I get S3 access. Planning to test on both q4_0 path and an FP16 fallback. Should have initial results within 24-36h.

Maya (Sales): Umbra also asked about SLA: they want p95 < 250ms for single-token streaming. Can we commit for Dedicated?

Ethan (SE): p95 < 250ms single-token is aggressive for 30B when using batch size 1 on mid-tier GPUs. On A10g-class we might hit ~180-220ms for short sequences if KV cache warm; on cold path p95 could spike. We should propose a realistic SLA: 250ms p95 for steady-state with warm KV and recommended dedicated sizing. Call that out in the doc.

Jamal (Security): From compliance perspective, we should provide the standard SOC2 attestation and offer a security workshop. I'll volunteer to join the call with Umbra's InfoSec.

Ava (Legal): I'll draft the SOW appendix for retention, IP, and deletion flow. Need the exact POC duration and expected data flows.

Maya (Sales): Thanks team. Action items:
- Ethan: run compat tests + upload results (24-36h)
- Priya: prepare adapter estimate and kernel-risk note (1 business day)
- Jamal: prep SOC2 + security workshop invite (2 business days)
- Ava: draft SOW appendix template (2 business days)
- Maya: confirm KMS/peering requirement with Umbra + send sanity script now

Ethan (SE): copying the ticket checklist I'll use: tokenizer-check, kv-schema, quant-kernel-compat, latency matrix, fallback FP16 run.

Maya (Sales): Umbra replied in ticket: they require KMS and private peering. I'll escalate to product for Private deployment feasibility.

Priya (ML Eng): If Private is required, onboarding time increases by ~3-5 days for infra setup + security review. Flagging so sales knows potential schedule slip.

Maya (Sales): Noted, will set expectations with Umbra.

Jamal (Security): I'm available for the call tomorrow at 10am PT.

Ava (Legal): I'll send a redline-ready SOW appendix draft by EOD tomorrow.

Ethan (SE): Starting tests now (pulling artifact). Will post a short log snippet to the ticket.

Priya (ML Eng): If we hit a kernel blocker, we can also propose a temporary model shim: run a small conversion container that interprets their quant format into an intermediate that our runtime accepts. That adds complexity but is a pragmatic fallback.

Maya (Sales): Perfect. I'll loop in the customer success manager after initial compat pass. :thumbsup:

Ethan (SE): Uploaded initial tokenization diff and one warmup run (see ticket). Token counts align but special tokens mismapped -> sending adapter patch next.

Maya (Sales): Great progress, thanks everyone.
